children: Awaysis' revenue rose year over year, driven by higher commission income, expanded short-term rental operations, increased resort asset utilization and growth in service revenue. Its net loss narrowed, principally on increased commission, rental and management income, partly offset by costs of scaling hospitality operations and preparing for capital raising.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss”. ³ Reported as “Basic and diluted net loss”.
: Growth reflected commission income, expanded short-term rentals, higher resort asset utilization and service-based revenue.
: Units were about 70% complete; completion and availability for sale or rental were expected by March 2027.
: The past 12-month rental average occupancy rate was about 12% as of September 30, 2026.
: Management forecast approximately $1.72 million in cash inflows and $1.41 million in outflows over 12 months, projecting net cash flows of about $315,400.
